solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tell, when brought before head? It offers security of various kinds (8, two words)

definitions.text: It offers security of various kinds

parts.note: to split on someone is to tell on them, to inform
a cap is what goes on the head, and the top of a thing is its cap

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put on a hat, then promised all-round protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like an instruction to speak, but it is the informer's verb. Split cap is short for split capital trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A split capital investment trust issues several different classes of share, so it offers investors more than one kind of security.

clue.text: Boer transport to block other vehicles circling junction? (11, two words)

parts.note: to scotch a wheel is to block it with a wedge

indicators.note: to circle something is to go all the way round it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: cars are vehicles other than the carts in the answer
a T-junction is named for the letter's shape

explanation.surface: A Boer wagon is driven to obstruct traffic going round a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that junction gives only the letter of the T-junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch carts were the heavy two-wheeled ox carts used by Boer settlers in South Africa.

clue.text: Road hazard mostly Scots endure after work's reversed

indicators.note: after puts the Scots word second, following the piece named later in the clue
something reversed runs the other way, so this short word is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
thole is a Scots and northern word meaning to endure or put up with

explanation.surface: A Scotsman puts up with a bad road surface after roadworks are undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' belongs to the definition: these holes are mostly a road hazard, but the word also names a cave shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hole in a road surface that damages vehicles, and also a deep cave shaft, hence mostly.

clue.text: Local units (monetary), Armenian primarily

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of each preceding word is used

parts.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A description of the small change used locally, in Armenia above all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the initials spell the word, and the clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The luma is an Armenian coin, one hundredth of a dram, so it is a local monetary unit there.

clue.text: They grant authority to Crown investigators, upsetting Ironside about new Queen

definitions.text: They grant authority to Crown investigators

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the others
upsetting a thing knocks it over and into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Crown investigators unsettle the detective Ironside over a fresh queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironside was a TV detective, which suits the investigators, but here the name is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquirendo is a legal commission empowering someone to make inquiry on the Crown's behalf, so these documents authorise investigators.

clue.text: Edible bulb, coloured, on top of heap

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for coloured
to amass is to heap up

explanation.surface: A coloured bulb sits on top of a pile of others.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on top of' puts the first piece above the second. 'Heap' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Camass is a North American plant of the lily family whose bulbs were eaten by Native Americans.

clue.text: It's posted by admirer, youngster that's burning inside?

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other, which wraps round it

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, or a cheeky youngster
a fire that is still burning is said to be in

explanation.surface: A young fan, burning with ardour, posts a picture of their idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning inside' suggests passion; it is the word for a lit fire placed within the youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a picture of an admired star pinned to a wall, so a fan puts it up.

clue.text: Stamp with foot running lap round gym

indicators.note: round puts the jumbled letters on both sides of the other piece
running suggests letters moving about, so their order changes

parts.note: taken as written
PE, physical education, is the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: A runner pounds the ground while lapping the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamp' could be a postage stamp, but it is the fencer's foot movement.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing an appel is a sharp stamp of the leading foot, used as a feint or warning.

clue.text: After delay I appear, paid to come round, taken from others' work

indicators.note: coming round something means enclosing it, so this piece wraps the rest

parts.note: PD is the abbreviation for paid
a lag is a delay
taken as written
to arise is to appear or come up

explanation.surface: A late performer arrives, having been paid, to come round after the wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I appear' after 'delay' builds the middle in order; the abbreviation for paid then goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarised writing is copied from someone else's work and passed off as one's own.

clue.text: Inspiration for heroic opera record turning up — does it culminate in bloomer?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Spanish hero El Cid inspired Massenet's opera Le Cid
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record of a heroic opera turns up, and the question is whether it ends in a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer looks like a blunder; here it is a flowering plant, and the stalk ends in its bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicle is a small stalk, such as the one bearing a single flower, so it ends in a bloom.

clue.text: Unfledged bird always reared in centre of nest

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
the centre of a word is its middle, so only those letters are used

parts.note: the two middle letters

indicators.note: reared means raised up, and in a down clue a raised word reads from the bottom

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A young bird that has always been raised in the middle of the nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reared' sounds like bringing up chicks, which suits the nest, but it turns the word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyas is a young hawk taken from the nest for falconry before it can fly.

clue.text: Company stationery perhaps, one allowing varied shade

parts.note: a letter is one who lets, that is allows

indicators.note: something varied has been changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm's notepaper, perhaps the kind that comes in several tints.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is not mail but one who lets, a landlord or anyone permitting something.
explanation.definitionFit: Letterheads are sheets printed with a firm's name and address, so they are business stationery.

clue.text: No. 1 in charts available for sale, including new number

indicators.note: number one in a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a new book or record that is out can be bought
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A chart-topping record is now in the shops, with a new track added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 1 in charts' looks like a hit single, but it takes only the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a total reached by counting, so it is a number.

clue.text: Channel for ground grain, distance about 80 yards (or more)

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a mile is a distance
a ley or lea is a measure of yarn: 80 yards for worsted, longer for other yarns

explanation.surface: A grain channel described as running some distance, about eighty yards or more.
explanation.walkthrough: The yardage looks like the length of the channel; it is the textile measure. The distance splits after its first three letters to take it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill-eye is the opening in a mill casing through which the ground meal comes out.

clue.text: Convert (in a way) disturbed at CE rite after mass

indicators.note: after sends the jumbled letters second, behind the single letter named at the end

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A convert is upset by a Church of England service that follows Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' looks like a noun, a new believer, but it is the verb; 'mass' is the physics symbol, not the service.
explanation.definitionFit: To metricate is to switch measurements to the metric system, one particular kind of converting.

clue.text: Hazel's pretty pendants, ornamental in large measure

indicators.note: in large measure means most of the word is used, so the letters sit inside it

parts.note: the letters run inside this word, leaving out its first three and last one

explanation.surface: The hazel's hanging flowers are largely decorative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ornamental' reads as describing the pendants, but its middle holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenta is the plural of amentum, a catkin, and hazel catkins hang like pretty pendants.

clue.text: Misled about gold, might trust a 'miracle-worker'

indicators.note: about means around, so the other letters surround the metal
misled means led astray, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone fooled by talk of gold may trust a so-called miracle-worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaumaturgist works wonders or magic, from the Greek for marvel-worker.

clue.text: Stripy fish, caught by sorcery?

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
obia is a variant spelling of obeah, West Indian sorcery

explanation.surface: A striped fish, landed by magic.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobia is a large game fish of warm seas with dark horizontal stripes along its sides.

clue.text: Shaver mostly made to divide half of sweet exactly — it's very hard

indicators.note: dividing something splits it in two, so this piece goes in the middle
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a bonbon is a sweet

indicators.note: taking half of a word discards the other half

parts.note: a razor is a shaver
surface padding that also confirms the halving: the sweet's two halves are identical

explanation.surface: A shaver is jammed into a sweet and proves too tough to bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exactly' is fair because the sweet's two halves are identical, so either half gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Borazon is boron nitride, an industrial abrasive almost as hard as diamond.

clue.text: Opening sought by marketing men, kind that's hard getting in

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: kind and nice both mean pleasant to others
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Marketers look for an opening, a nice one that is hard to break into.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a gap in the market, a specialised opening that marketers try to fill.

clue.text: Cocotte? This woman's filled with wild lust

indicators.note: filled with means holding something inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: her refers to this woman

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kept woman, described as full of unbridled desire.
explanation.walkthrough: A cocotte is also a cooking pot, but here it is the old word for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocotte is a dated French term for a prostitute, and hustler is a slang word for one.

clue.text: Left-overs? Recipe I used cooking with one

indicators.note: cooking alters ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions
taken as written
taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether a recipe used up the remains of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes left-overs look like food; the answer is the general Latin plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Residua is the plural of residuum, a remainder or residue left after a process.

clue.text: Relieve of local tax under a tenancy in part

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the words is used, so the letters sit within them

parts.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: A tenant is partly freed from paying council tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the British local property tax before council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To derate is to exempt a property from paying rates, the old British local tax.

clue.text: Asteroid string by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means judging by what is heard, not by spelling

parts.note: a series is a string of things in succession

explanation.surface: An asteroid trailing a string, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres, the first asteroid discovered, is the largest body in the asteroid belt, now classed as a dwarf planet.

clue.text: Facile, not born in the States, they're not much to look at!

definitions.text: they're not much to look at!

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: US is the United States

indicators.note: not born means the abbreviation for born is taken away

parts.note: facile and glib both mean slick and superficial; b is born

explanation.surface: Superficial types who are foreign-born in America are called unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit named for its lumpy, unappealing skin, which the exclamation mark enjoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglis are wrinkled, blotchy citrus fruits whose very name admits they are not much to look at.

clue.text: Cheeky underling turned hearts

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a serf is a feudal underling
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: An impudent junior turned the hearts in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh is informal for impertinent or forward, the same as cheeky.

clue.text: A trendsetter

parts.note: read plainly: someone who starts a fashion
the setter's reading is the same: this is a bare definition with no wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: This is Azed's competition word: it is given only a plain definition, and readers send in their own cryptic clues for it, so there is no wordplay to find.
explanation.definitionFit: An avant-gardiste belongs to the avant-garde, the innovators whose new styles others later follow.

clue.text: Something like conductor's baton, length reduced in composition of Ravel

indicators.note: a composition is something put together anew, so the letters are rearranged
reduced by a length means the abbreviation for length is removed

parts.note: taken as written; l is length

explanation.surface: A conductor shortens a Ravel piece, wielding the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel the composer suits the conductor, but the name is only letters; 'composition' is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vare is a wand or staff of office, rather like a baton carried as a sign of authority.

clue.text: Example of the blues is devastating to the ears

indicators.note: to the ears means as heard, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: an army that sacks a town is devastating it

explanation.surface: A blues song is shattering to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: The blues look like music, which suits the ears, but they are shades of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxe blue is a light greyish-blue, so saxe is one of the many blues.

clue.text: Alluvial deposits from lake filled round fringes

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards
fringes here is a verb: to fringe something is to border it on both sides

parts.note: sated means filled up, satisfied
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Silt washed from a lake builds up round its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringes' looks like a noun, the lake's edges, but it is the verb that wraps the reversed word round the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Deltas are fan-shaped tracts of silt laid down at river mouths, so they are alluvial deposits.

clue.text: Palm tree root shifted relative position

indicators.note: shifted means moved about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written
the lie of something is how it is placed relative to its surroundings

explanation.surface: A palm tree's root has moved out of position.
explanation.definitionFit: The troolie, or bussu, is a South American palm whose huge leaves are used for thatch.

clue.text: Vatican hall excluding RA, troubled

parts.note: V is the international code for Vatican City

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out, so those two letters are removed

parts.note: an exedra is a classical recess or hall with seating
taken as written: these two letters are the ones removed

explanation.surface: The Vatican's hall is upset at not including a Royal Academician.
explanation.walkthrough: RA suggests the Royal Academy, which suits the art in the Vatican; it is just two letters to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexed means annoyed or worried, much as troubled does.

clue.text: Variant of disputed Shakespearean term: note received interpretation

indicators.note: received means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sese is a variant of sessa, a word in King Lear whose meaning is disputed
N is short for note

explanation.surface: A scholar offers a reading of a contested word in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The scholarly front half reads like the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: The sense of a passage is its meaning, which is what an interpretation sets out.

clue.text: One among contemporaries of Auden, W. H? They're exhausting

definitions.text: One among contemporaries of Auden, W. H?
definitions.note: Auden is one among the Spenders, a playful plural
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Stephen Spender was Auden's friend and contemporary, so Auden counts as one of the Spender set
second meaning: people who use up, or exhaust, money or resources

explanation.walkthrough: The query treats the poet's surname as a plural, so W. H. Auden is one of the Spenders. 'Exhausting' looks like tiring; it means using up.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenders use up money or supplies, which is to exhaust them, and Spender names Auden's poet friend.
